key_insight: Engineered surfaces require hierarchical, multi-modal NDE that pairs rapid screening with calibrated confirmation of surface and interface defects.
engineering_relevance: Matching inspection physics to coatings, deposits, and modified layers can support assessment of adhesion, porosity, residual stress, and service-critical damage.
method: Review electromagnetic, thermal, ultrasonic, optical, and radiographic inspection methods.
Link method capabilities and limitations to specific surface and interface problems.
Assess in-process sensing, data fusion, physics-informed machine learning, and digital twins.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a review of inspection capabilities and limitations, but reports no quantitative validation or detection-performance results.
watch_item: Deployment requires stronger probability-of-detection evidence, transferable models, reference specimens, and clear acceptance criteria.
paper_title: Non-Destructive Evaluation for Engineered Surfaces: Methods, In-Process Sensing, and Data-Driven Inspection in the NDE 4.0 Era
